economicsInterpretation.observation: The hardest option group has reusable subject evidence for 14 of 15 named requirements without paid content. Five are already source-covered candidates; nine need bounded specialist synthesis. One named model, Prochaska's six stages, remains a genuine rights-safe source gap after convenient NC sources were rejected.
economicsInterpretation.consequence: The source-first hypothesis remains viable, but specialist options have a higher source-fragmentation/manual-search cost than the representative compulsory topic. Automation should therefore optimise targeted source discovery and rights verification rather than assume one-textbook coverage.
economicsInterpretation.nextStep: Review option groups 1 and 2 at the same named-requirement level, then calculate whole-course option coverage before deciding whether to source the final narrow gaps or create original bridges.
